{{short description|Japanese mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2020}}
{{nihongo|'''Kumiko Nishioka'''|西岡 久美子|Nishioka Kumiko|extra=born 1954}} is a Japanese [[mathematician]] at [[Keio University]]. She specializes in [[transcendental number]]s, and is known for her research related to the theory of [[Mahler function]]s<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.encyclopediaofmath.org/index.php/Mahler_method|title=Mahler method - Encyclopedia of Mathematics|accessdate=8 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Fernandes|first=Gwladys|issue=6|journal=Annales de l'Institut Fourier|mr=3897974|pages=2553–2580|title=Méthode de Mahler en caractéristique non nulle: un analogue du théorème de Ku. Nishioka|url=https://aif.cedram.org/item?id=AIF_2018__68_6_2553_0|volume=68|year=2018|doi=10.5802/aif.3216|doi-access=free|arxiv=1707.08033}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Komatsu|first=Takao|doi=10.4064/aa-86-4-305-324|issue=4|journal=Acta Arithmetica|mr=1659089|pages=305–324|title=On inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation and the Nishioka-Shiokawa-Tamura algorithm|volume=86|year=1998|doi-access=free}}</ref> and [[Painlevé transcendents]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Casale|first=Guy|isbn=978-2-85629-263-1|issue=323|journal=Astérisque|mr=2647966|pages=83–100|title=Une preuve galoisienne de l'irréductibilité au sens de Nishioka-Umemura de la première équation de Painlevé|year=2009}}</ref> In 1996 she published the first comprehensive text on transcendence of Mahler functions, ''Mahler Functions and Transcendence'', extending and generalizing [[Mahler's method]].<ref>{{cite journal|author-first=Alf|author-last=van der Poorten|author-link=Alf van der Poorten|title=Review of ''Mahler Functions and Transcendence'' by Kumiko Nishioka|url=https://academic.oup.com/blms/article-abstract/30/6/663/302097|year=1998|journal=Bull. London Math. Soc.|volume=30|issue=6}}</ref> Her husband Keiji Nishioka is also a mathematician, and a coauthor.
